title: Fun Quarter performs traditional rites to protect the land
excerpt: At the start of October 2026 the Quarter Head of Fun led the men of the quarter in traditional rites to protect the land and drive away wrongdoers.
sourceNote: Written fresh on 17 October 2026 from the Mbengwi Info Newsline post of 8 October 2026. The post dates the rites to 'Monday 6th October 2026', but 6 October 2026 was a Tuesday, so the day is given here only as the first week of October. The Quarter Head is named as the report names him; the Indigenes register records a 'Fodom Calvin' as quarter head of Fun, and whether these are one man is not established, so no link is made between them. Rewritten 17 October 2026 in the community's voice; date and identity caveats kept in R-072.
body:
At the start of October 2026, the men of Fun Quarter went back to the roots to protect their land. Led by the Quarter Head of Fun, Mr Nji Calvin, they carried out traditional rites to guard the village and chase away evil-doers.

The rites came at a worrying time. Theft, burglary and violent crime have been rising across Meta, and Guneku has not been spared: young men accused of stealing and raping were recently arrested in the village, and a house close to PC Fun was broken into, its window smashed and property carried away. Our Palace's handling of one of these cases is reported here: Our Palace questions suspects after an attack on a family.

Through the rites, the traditional authorities of Fun called on the powers of the land against those who steal, kill and rape. As one voice in Guneku put it, the land will no longer tolerate strangers, or sons of the soil, who have chosen crime as a way of life. Other villages in Meta have taken similar steps in recent weeks.

The rites were held on Monday 5 or Tuesday 6 October. Mbengwi Info Newsline, which reported them on 8 October, gave the date as “Monday 6th October”, and the two do not match.

More about the quarter: Fun.
